name: Drum Bus Plate
description: A second of plate a little narrowed, with the kick's lows kept out of it: it glues a kit together without washing it out.

name: Guitar Plate
description: Under two seconds, narrowed and darker, with a short pre-delay: a guitar keeps its place and gains a tail.

name: Long and Bright
description: The damper drawn well back: four seconds in the lows and a shimmering top, its lows cut so a long tail does not muddy the mix. For ballads and slow pads.

name: Send, All Wet
description: The plate alone, for a return track that several tracks are sent to, at the decay a studio's plate was most often left at.

name: Short and Dark
description: The damper pressed close and the highs cut: under a second of warm plate that thickens a sound without being heard as reverb.

name: Snare Plate
description: A short, bright plate for a snare drum: the whip of the highs comes with the hit and the tail is gone before the next one.

name: Strings, Lush
description: Three and a half seconds on the middle plate, which keeps the whip of every mode up to 1.5 kHz, held back 40 ms: strings and piano bloom into it.

name: Vocal Plate
description: Two seconds of plate behind a voice, held back 30 ms so the words come first, with its lows and its very top taken off so it sits behind them.

name: Whole Plate, Damper Open
description: Every mode of the sheet, all twenty-seven thousand, with the damper as far away as it goes: nearly five seconds in the lows. It costs ten times what the light plate does; for a return track or a final mix.
